title: Bar exam review III: essays, performance tests and the NextGen exam
audience: a law graduate preparing for a U.S. bar exam (the Uniform Bar Exam or the NextGen bar exam)
purpose: Write timed bar essays and performance tests, answer NextGen integrated question sets and performance tasks, build exam-day timing and stamina, and understand character and fitness review and the licensing steps.
primary_reading: NCBE: exam information, content outlines and sample materials

weeks.1: How written bar answers are graded
weeks.2: IRAC under time: organizing an essay
weeks.3: Essay practice: contracts, torts and property
weeks.4: Essay practice: business associations, estates and family law
weeks.5: The performance test: reading the file and the library
weeks.6: Writing the performance test: memos and briefs
weeks.10: Character and fitness and the licensing process

blocks.deliverable: Write two timed essays and self-grade with a model answer.
Week 7 midterm; complete an integrated set and a performance task under time.
Plan exam week and complete a licensing checklist.
Complete a full written session under time and repair weak areas.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Simulated written session: complete two supplied essays and one performance test under strict timing, self-grade with the supplied rubrics, and write a final repair plan.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
